title: Methods Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Plan an investigation, then defend it against an examiner. Practise the choices that pick up methods marks.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam stretch on planning a research study, choosing methods and evaluating bias.
final_note: A great methods answer makes a clear choice, justifies it, then names one limitation.

concepts.def: Subjects change behaviour because they are watched.
Personal views shaping how data is collected.
Treats sociology like a science seeking laws.
Studies meanings people give to actions.
Small trial run to test the method first.

walkthroughs.body_html: Want statistics on truancy? Use a structured questionnaire (positivist, reliable). Want to understand why pupils truant? Use unstructured interviews (interpretivist, valid). Top answers explain both.
If participants know they are watched they may behave differently (Hawthorne effect), lowering validity. Researcher bias can creep into question wording. Triangulation and pilot studies reduce both.
'I would use X because...'. Add: 'A strength is... A limit is... I would also use Y to triangulate'. Always link to the topic, e.g. studying gang membership needs snowball and covert observation.

mcqs.q: The Hawthorne effect lowers which quality of data?

numericals.q: How many methods are usually combined when 'triangulating' research?

free_texts.q: What two-word term names a small trial run of your method before the real study?
